children: was trading lower as BofA Securities cut its recommendation on the stock to Neutral from Buy after the Federal Housing Finance Agency decided to place VantageScore 4.0 and Classic FICO on the same LLPA pricing grid.
Shares were down 2.73% to $601.00 during pre-market trading on Wednesday.

"The move removes a key distinction between the models, and follows a series of regulatory developments that may challenge FICO's historically dominant mortgage market position, including a VS pilot and full VS approval for confirming loans in Sept," said analysts Curtis Nagle and Ryan Rivera.

"While the pace of lender adoption remains uncertain, we believe the revised grid adds another risk to score volumes, pricing, and market share, on top of less leeway on headline Score price increases given high and persistent regulatory scrutiny," said the research note.

"At the same time, FICO 10T and the Direct Lender Program (DLP), which provides new optionality on pricing, await regulatory approval. Other potential monetization initiatives are being considered but uncertain in timing and extent," said the note.
The price objective on FICO was halved to $700.00 from $1,400.00.

title: Fair Isaac cut to Neutral from Buy after FHFA removes key distinction from VantageScore
